title: Umm Ma'bad's goat
hook: the sirah tells of a thin goat in a woman's tent giving milk when he touched it

segments.voice: Yesterday, Suraqa rode after the reward until his horse sank. Your line was: the sand held him back. Which chase did you let go of? Day seven hundred sixty-nine.

Dust, heat, and a tent on the road north. The travelers are hungry. They stop at the tent of a woman the sirah calls Umm Ma'bad, a woman known for giving food and water to people passing by. They ask if she has meat or dates to sell. She has nothing. It has been a hard, dry season, and the flock is out grazing. All that's left at the tent is one goat, too thin and weak to go out with the others. This is not a story from Bukhari or Muslim. It comes from the sirah and from other collections. Today: Umm Ma'bad.
screen: `A TENT ON THE ROAD.` → `NOTHING TO SELL.` → `ONE THIN GOAT.`

segments.voice: In the story, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, notices the goat at the side of the tent. He asks Umm Ma'bad about it. She says it was too weak to go with the flock. He asks: does the goat have any milk? She says the goat is far too worn out for that. He asks her permission to milk her anyway. And her answer is lovely: if you see milk in her, then milk her. He rubs the goat's udder, says the name of Allah, and prays, and the milk comes. He calls for a vessel. Umm Ma'bad drinks first, then his companions, then he drinks last. He milks again and leaves the vessel full for her. Then they ride on. See who drinks first. The host, who had nothing to give, is served first. The guest who brought the milk drinks last. Later her husband, Abu Ma'bad, comes home driving the thin flock and sees the full vessel. Where did this come from? And she describes the man who stopped by, his face, his eyes, his voice, and her description is kept with the story. A woman with nothing to offer becomes a witness. The story doesn't send her a feast. It takes the one weak thing at the edge of the tent, the goat everyone had given up on, and draws enough from it for everyone. Then the travelers ride on. Tomorrow they reach the edge of Yathrib.
screen: `IF YOU SEE MILK IN HER, MILK HER.` · `THE HOST DRINKS FIRST.` · `A FULL VESSEL LEFT BEHIND.` · `SHE BECOMES A WITNESS.` · then, large: `FROM THE DRY GOAT, MILK.`

segments.voice: The practice: share from little. Sit, and breathe slowly. Think about something you have only a little of today. Time, patience, money, energy, a kind word. Notice the voice that says: not now, there isn't enough. Then think of one person who could use a small share of it. Not the whole thing. A cup's worth. Picture handing it to them first, before yourself. If you pray, you can ask Allah to put a blessing in what little you have. Stay with that person in mind. The bell holds the time.
Umm Ma'bad. In the sirah, the thin goat left behind at her tent gives milk when the Prophet milks it, enough for everyone, with the vessel left full. Today's word.
Your line: from the dry goat, milk. Today, give a cup's worth of something you're short on, and let someone else drink first. Day seven hundred sixty-nine.

original.note: Arabic: 'mother of Ma'bad', the name she is known by in the sirah.

trapdoor: what you thought: a miracle story about a goat.
what it means: the host with nothing is served first, and the weakest thing at the tent becomes enough for all.
what a scholar hears: reported outside Bukhari and Muslim, by Ibn Sa'd, al-Hakim and others; her description of the Prophet is part of the same report.

sources.ref: The report of Umm Ma'bad (Ibn Sa'd, al-Tabaqat; al-Hakim, al-Mustadrak; al-Tabarani)

notes: The Umm Ma'bad report is outside Bukhari and Muslim; scholars differ on the strength of its chains. The script says it comes from the sirah and other collections and that Muslims have told it a long time. Confirm framing.
Collections named in the trapdoor and sources (Ibn Sa'd, al-Hakim, al-Tabarani) cited from memory; confirm.
The order of drinking (she first, companions, then the Prophet last) and the vessel left full follow common retellings; confirm.
Index hook says 'an old woman'; script avoids giving her age. Confirm.
'A woman known for giving food and water to passers-by' follows common retellings; confirm.
